item.title: SCP Idea: Re: SCP Idea
item.content:encoded:
You're going to have to give someone a lot more detail here before they can tell whether this idea is interesting: remember, you have 400 words to use to explain this.

Hermit crabs that do weird things.

Strange hermit crabs that seem to be connected in an anomalous way

Like, connected in an anomalous way how? What weird things do they do? Why does them having killed people in Naples, Florida matter? What's the actual story you're telling within this SCP?

Despite giving very little detail, this feels kinda reminiscent of SCP-5915 but at the moment, that's only because 'death', 'gulf of mexico' and 'hermit crabs' and it's very possible you're taking this in a completely different direction.

item.title: SCP Idea Seeks Greenlight: Re: SCP Idea Seeks Greenlight
item.content:encoded:
[+] Open for critique
– hide block

Small items may be offered as 'tribute' to prevent the doll's nature from taking important concepts/people.

What do you mean by 'taking' here? Is this like…a semantic hazard which might take the meaning of 'freedom' so no-one understands what it means anymore? Or is this more a small scale thing where it might take the concept of freedom which allows it to be free/to be interpreted as free?

To remain generally inert, the item must receive a tribute every 2-3 days.

I'm, generally not a fan of SCPs that like, force the Foundation to interact with them in this way; it's generally more interesting (at least to me) if they willingly choose to do something because then it opens you up to asking the question 'why did they choose to do this'.

This doll embodies Otaku obsession culture and gatekeeping culture as satire, giving a supernatural explanation for such phenomena.

As a satire, this feels…off? It doesn't so much satirise the phenomenon as just, repeat it verbatim but with a supernatural cause. This isn't necessarily an issue alone though.

The core of my concern with this proposal is that we have this interesting start to the story: the discovery of the anomaly, the identification of the otaku, the thing coming into foundation contact; but I don't know where all these individual parts go: what do you do with them all? How do you explore the idea of obsessive culture and otaku-ness and gatekeeping in this? What conclusions do you draw about it? Where do the interviews and the found footage take this narratively?

I have some concerns about the compulsive nature of this, it feels to me that the doll somehow inspiring the creation of otakus without forcing people to become them would be more interesting: it'd really let you like, explore why some people become so obsessive.

item.title: Sir Reginald: Re: Sir Reginald
item.content:encoded:
I'm somewhat interested in a fictional character manifesting and having to deal with it's "unreality"

But the whole "it possesses people and takes over bodies" and "makes anomalous weapons" things seems less interesting.

My advice would be to cut out those two things and make him literally a physical manifestation of the fictional character, who at first is confused and then starts having to deal with the fact that he's a character from a tv show. That psychological conflict is enough to carry the whole article. The other two things would only feel like distractions.

item.title: EVER EVASIVE BUBBLE!!! IN NEED OF GREENLIGHT!!!: Re: EVER EVASIVE BUBBLE!!! IN NEED OF GREENLIGHT!!!
item.content:encoded:
This feels thin, I think you need to develop your narrative more. What is the stakes? Why does the Foundation need to make a whole site around this one thing?

There aren't any characters, there's very little plot mentioned, and I don't see any thematic elements that you want to discuss.

What makes you interested in this? What do you want the reader to take away from it? How will your story be told? As this, as it stands, is not even a monster manual entry… as it has very little substantive details.

item.title: Memetic Instruction Pamphlets: Re: Memetic Instruction Pamphlets
item.content:encoded:
The whole "this anomaly makes you do bad things to other people" is so played out that I would be unlikely to find it particularly interesting. More so the whole "hidden group that knows more than the foundation and will be watching" brand new GoI.

I think at its core, this concept proposal shows that you know how to tell a story as the investigation sounds somewhat compelling but the core anomaly is sorta cliche…

I'd suggest going back to the drawing board as to the actual anomaly, because this just covers tropes that are too frequently leaned on in my opinion.

item.title: SCP-5640 The Stomach IDEA looking for greenlight: Re: SCP-5640 The Stomach IDEA looking for greenlight
item.content:encoded:
I agree with Cybersqyd's perspective below… I advised tying the anomaly to the political story, but then you've gone and sorta used this political story as just background for a weird thing

I'm much less interested in a story about something some horrible government used to silence dissidents that is really just about the Foundation studying something… I think this would be better served with less focus on the Foundation and more on the horrors of the anomaly.

If this is about disappeared folks, that's a heavy narrative theme right there… don't abandon it to focus on testing with cows. The testing wouldn't be nearly as engaging as a discussion of how this government used something so horrible to enact its disappearances.

Finally… as Sqyd said below, because this is a real situation where real people died and were vanished by a government, you have to be careful. You don't want to make this just an entertaining story… because you're talking about a great horror perpetrated in real life. So I would suggest focusing in on that, and using the article to discuss it in a way that is meaningful.

item.title: Incorporeal mass at the center of the Earth: Re: Incorporeal mass at the center of the Earth
item.content:encoded:
Thank you for the feedback. Some responses below.

+ Collapsed for brevity
- Close

If something was incorporeal in the core and then became corporeal, why would the core collapse?

It isn't simply more mass being added to the core, it is part of the core being replaced with the incorporeal objects, which are far less dense, allowing large amounts of additional matter to be pushed into the core in a large surge. it should also be noted that due to the nature of several types of intangibility there are several intangible corpse in a single place being expelled from each other while becoming corporeal, potentially causing large seismic disruptions due to the movement of large amounts of mass. As for the 'disastrous' aspect, that is what is being implied to happen in the scenario discussed at the end.

Don't do this, don't redact the size. It doesn't serve anything, do some research and figure out what sorta size you want to imply and just say it. Would be more impactful.

Fair enough, but what more impact would a unit of measure have? I am of the opinion that a well placed redaction can emphasize the horror of an article. To anyone who isn't familiar with the size of a human body or the size of the earths core a definitive amount I feel a definitive amount would lessen the impact. That being said, I may just blackbox the exact volume with a large amount of digits.

More of concern is the lack of narrative. There isn't an arc to this, its merely discussing the description of an anomaly. What is it you want to say with this article? What do you want the readers to take away from it? We can't really know what the people are going through as they sink to the center of the earth… so where is the human aspect of this anomaly?

You are correct in there not being a central narrative but for an anomaly of this type, there can't really be one, as it isn't the result of one central anomaly. The human aspect of this article comes in the form of the individual stories of the people down there, implied through their descriptions. Furthermore, due to the nature of certain types of intangibility some of the people are still alive and fully aware of there situation, but unable to do anything about it. Given that I am planning on having at least one of the people as a ghost, the foundation may be able to conduct an interview with them via use of a séance. Ending the article with the potential of disaster is meant to convey how this is truly a lose-lose situation, with them being stuck, us being doomed and neither party being able to do anything about it.

item.title: Around the world: Re: Around the world
item.content:encoded:
I don't mean to be harsh but the phrasing in the elevator pitch has me very confused. How would one look at a compas from 200 meters away? How big is this compass?

moreover, it feels a bit like a run of the mill "other dimension" exploration… I think what you need to do is add some character to both the other dimension and those who are going to be trapped there. What sort of story do you wanna play with here? is there a theme you're working with (other than, alternate universes)?

Keep in mind, the sky is the limit with anomalies and alternative universes… so what can you do to make this one stand out?

Additionally I would simplify the logic of how people are transported to this other dimension. Also You don't need to designate an observer as part of the SCP unless they're somehow changed. You could just say "individuals observing SCP-XXXX"

item.title: Te Horoi Pai (Seeking Greenlight): Re: Te Horoi Pai (Seeking Greenlight)
item.content:encoded:
I'm pretty lost as to why this anomaly leads to a disappearance… you describe it as a compulsive effect to spread the love for this product (summing up/paraphrasing) and then people vanish? Are the entities doing something to them?

Also, I have to say the whole "make a thing that forces you to spread it around so that hours later you're attacked by otherworldly entities" isn't the most straight forward of concepts.

Thematically, these entities seem discordant with a product that enhances a person's hygiene. What does that have to do with something representing "subconscious fetishes or extremest fears"? I'd also suggest being careful with the demonizing of "fetishes" because such things are subjective and often seen as "gross" from the outside but is in reality just another form of sexual orientation repression… Like a sexual practice you find uncomfortable doesn't equate that practice with extreme fear… suggesting those are interrelated is dicey at best.

item.title: The Bone Seer: Re: The Bone Seer
item.content:encoded: Hey there! I'm really glad you like the idea. I should point out that the K-class scenario is a claim of the SCP, not something we know will happen. item.title: Incorporeal mass at the center of the Earth: Re: Incorporeal mass at the center of the Earth
item.content:encoded:
Here are some minor quibbles with the internal logic you've presented:

+ show block
– hide block

causing part of it to become corporal before the unit is destroyed, causing part of the earths core to collapse in on itself, creating a minor earthquake.

Several things with this: a) If something was incorporeal in the core and then became corporeal, why would the core collapse? The core isn't hollow, its solid with liquified rock. Also, the core is made the way it is because of gravity pushing innumerable metric tons of matter into it, I can't imagine a little more would suddenly make it collapse even a teensy bit. More than likely that matter would then be vaporized by the intense heat and then some small amount of gas would escape the core potentially (but this is happening all the time). b) if part of the core were to collapse it wouldn't make a "minor earthquake" it would probably be disastrous.

The exact size of this mass is [REDACTED] by it is implied to be truly massive.

Don't do this, don't redact the size. It doesn't serve anything, do some research and figure out what sorta size you want to imply and just say it. Would be more impactful. Also in general, I am of the opinion that "redacted" information doesn't serve narratives in 99% of the case. Here isn't an exception to me.

More of concern is the lack of narrative. There isn't an arc to this, its merely discussing the description of an anomaly. What is it you want to say with this article? What do you want the readers to take away from it? We can't really know what the people are going through as they sink to the center of the earth… so where is the human aspect of this anomaly?

I think you should brainstorm concerning a narrative. Think about what sort of story you want to tell and come up with a way to tell it with this anomaly. Because at the end of the day, most articles that only concern themselves with "look at this weird phenomenon" don't do well. If you have some clever way to avoid using narrative to getting the reader engaged, I am not seeing it.
